world.title: Kampala Summit to Decide Fate of AU Mission as US Funding Cuts Bite
world.description: MOGADISHU – A series of high-level meetings in Mogadishu, Addis Ababa and Kampala are scrambling to secure the future of the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM), as the Trump administration’s decision to suspend a portion of its financial support has exposed the mission’s chronic funding crisis and raised urgent questions about Somalia’s readiness to assume full security responsibility. The consultations, which began earlier this month, have drawn together officials from the Federal Government of Somalia, the African Union, troop-contributing countries and international partners. A senior summit is scheduled for July 31 in Kampala, where a final decision on the mission’s financing and restructuring is expected. The outcome of that meeting will determine whether AUSSOM can continue to function, or whether the security gains of the past decade will begin to unravel. A Funding Crisis Decades in the Making AUSSOM, which officially replaced the African Union Transition Mission in Somalia (ATMIS) in January 2025, currently fields nearly 12,000 personnel operating under a reduced mandate focused on training, advising and institutional capacity building. The shift from direct combat support to a more targeted approach reflected a strategic recalibration, but it also came with a funding model that was never fully secured. The African Union projected a need for approximately $190 million in 2025 to facilitate the transition from ATMIS to AUSSOM. Civil society monitors have warned that short-term needs already exceed $90 million, with impacts ranging from unpaid troops to interrupted aid for at-risk groups. The European Union, which has been the mission’s longest-standing supporter, has committed €600 million to African-led efforts from 2022 to 2024, including €340 million for Somalia’s military operations.
